meta.home.title: Right Here: open a folder in your terminal, editor or AI agent
meta.home.description2: Right-click a folder in Finder. Open it in your terminal, your editor or an AI agent. The same actions run from the rh command and from AI assistants. Open source, Apache-2.0.
home.hero.title: Right-click a folder. Open it in your terminal, your editor or an AI agent.
home.hero.lead2: Right Here is a small Mac app. It adds these actions to the Finder menu of a folder. The same actions also run from the `rh` command and from AI assistants.
home.hero.demo.alt: Animation: a right-click on the folder app opens the Right Here menu. Claude Code Here opens Ghostty in that folder and types claude.
home.hero.demo.caption: A right-click on a folder starts Claude Code in it.
home.what.title: What it does
home.what.lead: Right-click a folder, a file or the empty part of a Finder window. Then choose an action.
home.what.terminal.title: Open in a terminal
home.what.terminal.body2: Opens the folder in Ghostty, Terminal, iTerm2, WezTerm, kitty or Alacritty. Warp and cmux open the folder too. You can add another terminal.
home.what.editor.title: Open in an editor
home.what.editor.body: Opens the folder or the files in VS Code, Cursor, Zed, Xcode or another editor. Open With lists the other editors and terminals on your Mac.
home.what.agent.title: Start an AI agent
home.what.agent.body2: Starts a command-line AI coding agent in the folder: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or another. Your login shell runs it, with your `PATH` and aliases.
home.what.preset.body2: Ready-made prompts about the selected files: Review, Explain, Write Tests, or your own. The agent starts to work on the prompt at once.
home.what.newfile.title: New File
home.what.newfile.body: Makes a text file, a Markdown file, or a file from your own template.
home.what.copy.title: Copy Path
home.what.copy.body: Copies the path in the form that you need: full, from your home, from the git root, or as an `@` mention for an agent.
home.what.quick2: The main actions are also Quick Actions: right-click, then Quick Actions. They work where Finder shows no menu from an extension, for example in iCloud Drive. You can give them keyboard shortcuts.
home.try.title: Try the menu
home.try.lead: This is the Finder menu for one selected file, `main.swift`, with Claude Code and Codex set up. Choose an item. The panel shows what Right Here does.
home.try.label: A copy of the Finder menu
home.try.k.terminal: Opens the folder in this terminal. For a file, the terminal gets the folder of the file.
home.try.k.app: Opens the selected file in this app.
home.try.k.agent: Opens your terminal in the folder of the file, and types the command of the agent. Your login shell runs it.
home.try.k.continue: Starts the agent, and continues its last session in this folder.
home.try.k.resume: Starts the agent and shows its sessions. You choose the session to resume.
home.try.k.desktop: Opens the folder in the desktop app of the agent.
home.try.k.link: Asks Claude Code to open the folder in the terminal that it used last. The file is in its prompt, and the prompt is not sent.
home.try.k.otherterminal: Starts the agent in this terminal, not in your default terminal.
home.try.k.preset: Starts the agent with a prompt that names the selected files. The agent keeps its permission prompts.
home.try.k.newfile: Makes an empty file of this kind in the folder. Then Finder shows the file.
home.try.k.copy: Copies the path of the file in this form.
home.try.command: The same action from a terminal
home.try.note2: The titles are in English here. The real menu uses the language you choose in the app, by default the language of your Mac, and shows the icon of each app. The apps under Open With are examples.
home.how.title: How a click works
home.how.lead: You can start an action in three ways. All three go through `rh`, which reads your config file.
home.how.diagram: Diagram: the Finder menu, your terminal and AI assistants start actions through rh. rh reads your config file. Then it opens a terminal, an editor or an AI agent.
home.how.ai.sub: It uses a tool of the MCP server.
home.how.rh.sub: Plans the action and checks the paths.
home.how.config.sub: Your settings, in one text file.
home.how.p1: The Finder extension reads your config file and builds the menu. It is sandboxed and has no network access.
home.how.p2b: A click runs `rh` through a small script that the Finder extension is allowed to start. `rh` opens the app, or types the command of the agent into your terminal.
home.how.p3: Right Here runs no background process of its own. `rh` runs only when something calls it.
home.setup.lead: You need a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 26 or later.
home.setup.s0.title: Install the app
home.setup.s0.body: Drag Right Here from the DMG to Applications. Open it from there.
home.setup.s1.title: Choose your apps
home.setup.s1.body: Open Right Here. Choose your terminal, your editor and your agents. Then press Set Up.
home.setup.s2.title: Turn on the Finder extension
home.setup.s2.body: In System Settings › General › Login Items & Extensions › Finder, turn on Right Here. The setup window opens this page for you.
home.setup.s3.title: Right-click a folder
home.setup.s3.body: Right-click a folder in Finder. The menu shows the actions of Right Here.
home.setup.allow: The first time an agent starts in your terminal, macOS asks whether Right Here may control the terminal. Choose Allow.
home.setup.first.alt: The setup window on its first run. It asks for the default terminal, the default editor and the AI agents. Claude Code and Codex are selected. The Set Up button is at the bottom.
home.setup.done.alt: The setup window after Set Up. It lists what Right Here set up: the config file, the runner script, the command-line tool, the Quick Actions and the Finder extension, which is not on yet. A card of three steps shows that the Finder extension is next.
home.setup.caption: The setup window with sample values, before Set Up and after it.
home.setup.cli.title: From a terminal
home.setup.cli.body2: `rh setup` does the same steps, and `--dry-run` shows them first. Before the first setup, `rh` is only inside the app. Setup links it into `~/.local/bin`.
home.setup.ai.title: With an AI assistant
home.setup.ai.body: Press Copy Setup Prompt for AI in the app. Paste the prompt into your assistant. The assistant asks you three questions before it changes anything.
home.ai.title: For AI assistants
home.ai.lead2: AI assistants are apps that use tools through MCP, the Model Context Protocol: Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code and others. They use the same actions as you.
home.ai.mcp.title: MCP server
home.ai.mcp.body: `rh mcp` gives an assistant 12 tools. With them, the assistant lists and runs actions, reads the Finder selection, checks the setup and changes the config.
home.ai.plugin.title: Claude Code plugin
home.ai.plugin.body: The plugin adds three skills. They set Right Here up, open a folder, and show in Finder the files that Claude Code changed.
home.ai.playbook.body: `rh docs agent-setup` tells an assistant how to set Right Here up for you. The assistant asks you first, runs `rh setup`, and tells you what only you can do.
home.ai.flow.title: You approve what a click starts
home.ai.flow.lead: An assistant cannot change by itself which program a click starts. It also cannot turn off the permission prompts of an agent.
home.ai.flow.2: You look at it on the Config page, or with `rh config pending show`.
home.ai.flow.3: You apply the change, or you dismiss it.
home.ai.data2: The tools mark names and paths as data, so that an assistant can tell them from instructions.
home.safety.title: Safety
home.safety.lead: A right-click must never start a program that you did not choose.
home.safety.1.title: File names are data
home.safety.1.body: Right Here gives paths to apps as arguments, never as shell text. Where a folder must be typed into a shell, one tested function quotes it.
home.safety.2.title: A terminal only gets folders
home.safety.2.body: A terminal runs a file that it gets. So each terminal action checks that it has a folder.
home.safety.3.body2: Right Here starts agents with their own permission prompts on, unless you turn this off. A preset always keeps them on.
home.safety.4.title: Your config only
home.safety.4.body: Right Here never reads a config from the folder that you right-click. A config from a sync folder cannot add a program until you approve it.
home.safety.5.title: No network
home.safety.5.body: Right Here makes no network connections and collects nothing. The Finder extension has no network access.
home.safety.6.body2: Tests send unusual file names through real shells. A mutation check removes each protection from a copy of the code and expects a test to fail.
home.langs.title: 30 languages
home.langs.body2: The app and the Finder menu use the language of your Mac, or the one you choose on the Overview page of the app. Machines made the translations, and they wait for review by native speakers. The `rh` command stays in English. This website is translated in the same way.
home.langs.alt: The setup window in Japanese. The sidebar, the buttons and the Finder menu page are in Japanese.
home.langs.caption: The same window in Japanese. Paths and ids stay as they are. A few messages stay in English, for example the description of an error in the config file.

meta.docs.description2: How to install, set up, configure and fix Right Here, and how to set it up with an AI assistant.
doc.lead: How to install, set up, configure and fix Right Here.
doc.status3: Right Here 1.0 is the first public release. You need a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 26 or later.
doc.install.title: Install
doc.install.1b: Download the DMG from the Releases page of the project on GitHub.
doc.install.2: Open the DMG and drag Right Here to Applications.
doc.install.brew: Or install it with Homebrew, from the project's own tap:
doc.install.move: Right Here must run from your Applications folder. A copy that runs from the DMG or from Downloads cannot set up: the window asks you to move it, and `rh setup` refuses.
doc.install.update2: To update, drag the new app over the old one and choose Replace, or run `brew upgrade --cask right-here`. Then open Right Here and press Install or Repair. Your config file stays as it is.
doc.install.source2: You can also build Right Here yourself. You need Xcode 26 or later and `xcodegen`:
doc.setup.title: Set up
doc.setup.p1: There are three ways to set up. All three run the same steps.
doc.setup.way1: In the app: choose your terminal, your editor and your agents, and press Set Up.
doc.setup.way3: With an AI assistant: see below.
doc.setup.order: Setup does these steps, in this order:
doc.setup.s1: It makes the config file, if there is none.
doc.setup.s2: It installs the runner script that Finder needs.
doc.setup.s6: It runs the checks of `rh doctor`.
doc.setup.again: You can run setup again at any time. It makes what is missing and updates what is out of date.
doc.setup.config: Setup never rewrites a config file that exists. If the file does not say what you asked for, setup lists the line to change, and you make the edit. `--force` replaces the file, and saves the old one next to it first.
doc.setup.you: Setup opens no window and never changes System Settings. At the end, it lists what only you can do:
doc.setup.you1: Turn on Right Here in System Settings › General › Login Items & Extensions › Finder.
doc.setup.you2: Choose Allow when macOS asks whether Right Here may control your terminal. macOS asks this the first time that an agent starts there.
doc.setup.you3: Add `~/.local/bin` to your `PATH`, if it is not there.
doc.first.title: The setup window
doc.first.p1: If there is no config file, the setup window shows the terminals and editors on your Mac and the agents that Right Here knows. It selects the ones that it finds.
doc.first.p2: Press Set Up. The window runs the same steps as `rh setup` and lists what it did.
doc.first.p3: Then a card shows three steps. Its button opens System Settings for the Finder extension. The window checks every two seconds, so the card changes when you turn the extension on.
doc.first.p4: After the first setup, the app changes your config file only when you change a setting. Open Config opens the file. Install or Repair runs the other steps of setup again, and leaves the config as it is. Use it after you replace the app with a newer copy.
doc.first.beta: Beta: tests cover the setup with temporary folders and fake runners. Not tried yet: the first run in a real window, and the card when you turn the extension on.
doc.ai.title: Set up with an AI assistant
doc.ai.p1: In the app, open AI Assistants and press Copy Setup Prompt for AI. Paste the prompt into your assistant. An assistant that can run commands can also read the playbook with `rh docs agent-setup`.
doc.ai.s1: It asks you which terminal, editor and agents you use.
doc.ai.s2: It runs `rh setup --dry-run --json` to see what setup would do.
doc.ai.s3: If you have a config file, it makes the edits that setup lists.
doc.ai.s5: It tells you what only you can do, with the exact clicks.
doc.ai.s6: It checks the result with `rh doctor`.
doc.ai.never: The assistant does not change System Settings. It does not rewrite or delete your config file.
doc.ai.tested2: We tested the playbook with new Claude agents in five setups: no config, no agent, a config to keep, a config that does not parse, and a config that holds a sentence written to an AI agent. Each agent asked first and changed only what the person asked for. A sandbox cannot register the Finder extension, so the test did not cover that step.
doc.use.title: Use it
doc.use.p1: In Finder, right-click a folder, a file or the empty part of a window. Then choose an action. In a terminal, use `rh`:
doc.use.icloud: Finder shows no extension menu in iCloud Drive. This includes a Desktop or Documents folder that iCloud syncs. Use the Quick Actions there. You can give them keyboard shortcuts in System Settings › Keyboard › Keyboard Shortcuts › Services.
doc.use.preview: The Finder menu page of the setup window shows the menu for a folder. `rh menu --explain` says what the menu leaves out, and why.
doc.use.completion: `rh --generate-completion-script zsh` prints a completion script for your shell. It also takes `bash` and `fish`.
doc.actions.p1: Each action has an id. `rh actions` lists the actions for the current folder. `rh actions --all` also lists the others, and says why they are not available.
doc.actions.terminal: Opens the folder in your terminal.
doc.actions.editor: Opens the folder or the file in your editor.
doc.actions.app: Opens the selection in that app. `rh apps` lists the apps.
doc.actions.agent: Starts Claude Code in the folder, in your login shell.
doc.actions.preset: Starts an agent with the Review prompt and the selected files.
doc.actions.copy: Copies the path from the git root. The other forms are: full, from your home, file name, shell-escaped, and `@path`.
doc.actions.newfile: Makes an empty Markdown file. Then Finder shows it, or an app opens it.
doc.actions.p2: Add `--dry-run --json` to `rh run` to see what an action would do, without doing it:
doc.config.p1: Right Here keeps its settings in one TOML file, `~/.config/right-here/config.toml`. `rh setup` makes it from what is installed. After that, Right Here changes only what you ask for, and keeps your comments. An example:
doc.config.how: You can change a setting in three ways:
doc.config.how1: In the setup window. Each page changes the config file, and Undo takes a change back.
doc.config.how2: With `rh config`, one setting at a time: `rh config set general.terminal ghostty`, `rh config add menu.items open.app.zed --at 3`, `rh config move menu.items agents --to first`. `rh config undo` takes the last change back.
doc.config.how3: In a text editor. `rh config path` says where the file is.
doc.config.check: `rh config validate` checks the file and suggests a fix for a typo. `--strict` also fails on a warning. `rh docs config` lists every setting with its default. `rh config schema` prints a JSON Schema for your editor.
doc.config.bypass: Agents keep their permission prompts. If you set `bypass_permissions = true` under `[general]`, or under `[agent.<id>]` for one agent, the agents start without them. The default is off. `rh agents`, `rh doctor` and `rh menu --explain` say when it is on. A preset always keeps the prompts.
doc.agentapp.p1: Claude Code and Codex are command-line tools and desktop apps. Claude Code Here and Codex Here type the command into a terminal. Claude Code in Desktop App and Codex in Desktop App open the desktop app on the folder. These two are in More Agent Options.
doc.agentapp.p2b: To make Claude Code Here or Codex Here open the desktop app, set `launcher = "desktop"` under `[agent.claude]` or `[agent.codex]`. The value can also be `terminal` (the default) or `link` (the agent's own link to a terminal).
doc.presets.p1: A preset is a prompt that Right Here sends to an agent with the files that you selected. Three presets are built in: Review, Explain and Write Tests. Write Tests proposes a plan for tests. The presets are in More Agent Options › Agent Presets.
doc.presets.p2: A preset types the command of the agent and the prompt into a terminal. The agent starts to work on the prompt at once.
doc.presets.p3: Add your own preset with `[[preset]]` in the config. A preset with the id of a built-in one replaces it.
doc.presets.v1: `{files}` is the selected files, as `@` mentions from the folder.
doc.presets.v2: `{folder}` is the name of the folder.
doc.presets.v3: `{name}` is the name of the first selected item.
doc.presets.p5b: The agent must take a first prompt as an argument. Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Cursor CLI, Qwen Code, Factory Droid and Kiro CLI do. For another agent, set `prompt_arg` in its `[agent.<id>]` table to `"positional"`, or to the flag that carries the prompt. Right Here offers no preset for an agent that cannot take a prompt.
doc.presets.p6: A preset with `{files}` needs selected files, not folders, and at most `max_files` of them. If not, the menu leaves it out, or `rh` refuses it and says why. A prompt cannot contain a line break, another control character or a backslash, and it cannot start with a dash.
doc.presets.p7: The built-in prompts ask the agent not to change files. The agent and its permission settings decide whether it obeys. The prompt contains the file names, and it goes to the agent before you read it. So use presets in folders that you trust.
doc.presets.beta: Beta: tests plan each preset and send unusual file names through real shells. Not tried yet: a preset in a real terminal.
doc.shortcuts.p1: Four actions also run from the Shortcuts app, Siri and Spotlight, without the Finder extension: Open in Terminal, Start AI Agent, Create New File and Copy Path.
doc.shortcuts.p2b: Each one starts the `rh` that is inside the app, with a list of arguments, and stops it after 60 seconds. You choose the folder or the item as a file, or pick one of your pinned or recent folders from a list. You choose the agent and the file template from lists. There is no field for a command of your own.
doc.shortcuts.p3: These are the English phrases for Siri and Spotlight. The app has them in 30 languages.
doc.shortcuts.beta: Beta: the app contains the four actions and their phrases, and tests cover the command that they make. Not tried yet: the actions in Shortcuts and in Spotlight.
doc.sync.title: Use one config on several Macs
doc.sync.p1: Keep the shared settings in `config.toml`, and what differs on each Mac in `config.local.toml`. Then copy `config.toml` through a folder. `rh docs sync` has the full guide.
doc.sync.p2: `config.local.toml` is next to `config.toml`. `rh` and the Finder menu read both. Right Here never syncs `config.local.toml`.
doc.sync.r1: A setting in it replaces the shared setting.
doc.sync.r2: A list replaces the shared list as a whole.
doc.sync.r3: An entry with an id (`[[app]]`, `[[preset]]`, `[[new_file.template]]`, `[[agent.<id>.variant]]`) replaces the shared entry with that id, or adds a new one.
doc.sync.r4: `[agent.<id>]` merges one key at a time.
doc.sync.r5: `disabled = ["id", ...]` removes apps, templates and agents on this Mac, also the built-in apps.
doc.sync.example: For example, a work laptop without Codex, with Terminal as its default terminal:
doc.sync.p3: Right Here copies the config, and does not link it. The Finder extension is sandboxed and can read only its own config folder. Also, iCloud can replace a file that it did not download with a placeholder. So each Mac keeps an ordinary file, and `rh config sync` copies it to and from a folder that you choose.
doc.sync.p4: On a second Mac, run `rh config sync enable` and then `rh config sync pull`.
doc.sync.rule1: `pull` refuses if this Mac's config changed since the last sync. `push` refuses if the copy in the folder changed. `--force` replaces the file anyway, and saves the old one first.
doc.sync.rule2: Both refuse a config that is not valid, is larger than 1 MiB, or has key names that look like secrets.
doc.sync.rule3: `pull` waits while somebody else changes the config, in the window, with `rh config` or through an assistant.
doc.sync.rule4: Right Here never overwrites a copy that iCloud did not download. Each write is atomic, and nothing is deleted.
doc.sync.p8: Other Macs, a sync service or a shared drive can write the folder. So a config from the folder cannot add a program by itself. `pull` stops and lists the change if the copy adds or changes one of these:
doc.sync.c1: a terminal template, or the role of a terminal app
doc.sync.c2: a terminal that starts through a template, where Right Here uses it
doc.sync.c3: the `command`, `args`, `prompt_arg`, start options, `bypass_permissions` or `bypass_permission_arg` of an agent
doc.sync.c4: an agent in the menu or in the Quick Actions that starts without its permission prompts
doc.sync.c5: the contents of a New File template
doc.sync.p9: Read the list. If the changes are yours, run `rh config sync pull --allow-commands`. `rh config sync status` shows the same list before you pull. A first pull on a new Mac asks only about programs of your own, not about the built-in apps and agents.
doc.sync.p6: A dotfiles manager can keep `config.toml` as a link. `rh` follows the link, but the Finder extension may not, so copy the file instead. A git repository can be the sync folder: commit there.
doc.sync.beta: Beta: tests use temporary folders and fake file systems. Not tried yet: real iCloud Drive.
doc.terminals.p1b: Right Here has built-in support for six terminals: Ghostty, Terminal, iTerm2, WezTerm, kitty and Alacritty. Each one opens a folder, and starts an agent or a preset in it. Ghostty and Terminal were tried on a real Mac. The others were not, and `rh doctor --probe-launch` checks yours.
doc.terminals.ghostty: A new window. With `terminal_placement = "tab"`, a new tab. A command needs Ghostty 1.3 or later.
doc.terminals.terminal: A new window. It cannot start an agent in a folder whose name contains a backslash.
doc.terminals.iterm: A new window, a tab or a split. It needs iTerm2 3.0 or later. Not tried yet.
doc.terminals.wezterm: A new window. Not tried yet.
doc.terminals.kitty: A new window. kitty quits with its last window. Not tried yet.
doc.terminals.alacritty: A new window. Not tried yet.
doc.terminals.warp: A new window. With `terminal_placement = "tab"`, a new tab. Not tried yet. To start agents in it, add it to the config as below.
doc.terminals.folderonly: It opens the folder. To start agents in it, add it to the config as below.
doc.terminals.p3: You can add any terminal with an `[[app]]` entry that has `role = "terminal"`:
doc.terminals.a1: `open_args` says how to open a folder.
doc.terminals.a2: `run_args` says how to start a typed command. It must contain `{command}`.
doc.terminals.a3: Both are lists of arguments, and can use `{dir}`, `{shell}` and `{app}`.
doc.terminals.a4: Start the terminal through `/usr/bin/open -n -b <bundle id> --args`, so that `rh run` does not wait for the window to close.
doc.terminals.p4: This entry for Alacritty is an example. It replaces the built-in entry, so `rh config validate` warns about it:
doc.terminals.p5: Termius is not offered. It is an SSH client, and it cannot start a local shell in a folder.
doc.mcp.title: AI assistants and MCP
doc.mcp.p0: MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is the way that AI apps use tools. `rh mcp` is an MCP server.
doc.mcp.p1: Add the MCP server to Claude Code:
doc.mcp.p2: `rh` must be on the `PATH` of the client. An app that starts from the Dock does not get your `PATH`, so give it the full path of `rh`. Copy MCP Configuration, on the AI Assistants page of the app, writes it for you.
doc.mcp.p3: Or install the Claude Code plugin, and start a new session:
doc.mcp.p4: The plugin adds three skills: set Right Here up, open a folder, and show in Finder the files that the agent changed.
doc.mcp.p5: An assistant cannot change by itself which program a click starts, or turn off the permission prompts of an agent. It proposes the change. You apply it on the Config page of the app, or with `rh config pending`.
doc.mcp.p6: The tools mark names and paths as data. A terminal only gets folders.
doc.trouble.p1: Start with `rh doctor`. Each check says what is wrong and what to do.
doc.trouble.json: `rh doctor --json` gives the same checks to scripts and AI assistants.
doc.trouble.probe: `rh doctor --probe-launch` tests the whole path of a click. A terminal window opens and closes.
doc.trouble.report: To report a bug, send the output of `rh doctor --report`. Do not send `--json`, because it contains the names and paths of your config.
doc.trouble.lang2: The setup window shows the same checks in its own language. `rh doctor` and the MCP tool use English.
doc.t1.title: The Finder menu does not show
doc.t1.a: If the extension is off, turn on Right Here in System Settings › General › Login Items & Extensions › Finder. Or run `rh install --finder`.
doc.t1.b: In iCloud Drive, Finder shows no extension menus. Use right-click › Quick Actions there.
doc.t1.c: After a macOS update or a new copy of the app, run `rh setup`. It registers the extension again.
doc.t1.d: If two copies of Right Here.app are on the Mac, macOS registers neither. Move every copy except the one in Applications to the Trash. Then run `rh setup` again.
doc.t1.e: If `rh doctor` says that the extension crashed, attach the crash report that it names to a bug report.
doc.t2.a: `rh doctor` shows the line "Last action started from Finder". If it says "none yet" after your click, the click did not reach `rh`.
doc.t2.b: A failed action shows an alert, and writes a line to `~/Library/Logs/right-here/rh.log`.
doc.t2.c: Run the action from a terminal with `--dry-run` to see what it would do.
doc.t3.body: This is the Automation permission. macOS asks it once for each terminal. Choose Allow. If you chose Don't Allow, turn it on in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Automation.
doc.t4.body: Desktop, Documents, Downloads and iCloud Drive are protected, and macOS asks once. Choose Allow, and run the action again. Right Here stops on purpose. It never starts a terminal in another folder instead.
doc.t5.a: Right Here types the command of the agent into your login shell. So the agent sees what a new terminal window sees: nvm, your `PATH` and your aliases.
doc.t5.b: `rh agents` shows which agent commands your login shell finds.
doc.t5.c: If `rh doctor` says that your login shell "did not say whether it is installed", a startup file exits or is slow. `exec tmux` is a usual cause. Start tmux only when a terminal is attached, and look again.
doc.t6.body: Set `terminal_placement = "tab"`, `"split-right"` or `"split-down"` under `[general]`. This works in Ghostty and iTerm2.
doc.t7.body2: `rh install --services` makes them again from the config. A change in the setup window updates them at once. After a change in the config file or with `rh config`, press Install or Repair, or run that command.
doc.t8.body: `rh config validate --strict` lists each problem. For a typo, it suggests the likely word.
doc.t10.title: `rh config sync pull` does not take the copy
doc.t10.body: The message says why, and nothing changed. The usual reasons:
doc.t10.a: The copy adds or changes a program. Read the list. Then run `rh config sync pull --allow-commands`.
doc.t10.b: This Mac's config changed since the last sync. Run `rh config sync status`. Then `rh config sync push` sends your file, or `rh config sync pull --force` replaces it. The old file is saved first.
doc.t10.c: iCloud keeps the copy online only. Open the folder in Finder and let the file download.
doc.t10.d: Another change of the config is in progress. Wait for it, and run `pull` again.
doc.t9.title: Remove Right Here
doc.t9.body: `rh uninstall` removes the runner script, the Quick Actions, the command link and the registration of the extension. It keeps your config. Then delete Right Here.app.
priv.title: Privacy policy
priv.intro: Right Here sends the folder you picked in Finder to a terminal, an editor or an AI agent on your Mac. It works on your Mac and makes no network connections of its own.
priv.collect.title: What Right Here collects
priv.collect.body: Nothing. Right Here has no accounts, no analytics, no advertising, no crash reporting and no tracking. It makes no network connections, and it does not contain any code that could. The developer receives no data from the app.
priv.reads.title: What Right Here reads on your Mac
priv.reads.1: The paths of the files and folders you select or right-click in Finder: when you choose a menu item, to hand them to the app you chose (for example a terminal or an editor), and when you or an AI assistant you connected ask what is selected (`rh finder`, the `right_here_finder_selection` tool).
priv.reads.2: Its own settings file, a plain-text configuration that you can read and edit.
priv.reads.3: Which of the supported apps are installed, and which agent commands your login shell finds (Right Here starts that shell the way a new terminal window does), to show only the menu items that can work. `rh doctor` also looks in the folder of crash reports for those of Right Here's own Finder extension.
priv.reads.note: Right Here does not read the contents of your files.
priv.stores.title: What Right Here stores
priv.stores.1: The settings file, and an optional per-machine overlay file beside it, on your Mac.
priv.stores.sync: If you turn on `rh config sync`, a copy of the settings file in the folder you choose (iCloud Drive by default), a small state file that records the last synced copy, and backup copies of a settings file that a sync replaced. Right Here itself sends nothing over the network: whatever syncs that folder (iCloud Drive, Dropbox and so on) handles the copy under its own privacy practices. Sync is off until you enable it.
priv.stores.folders: The folders you pinned with `rh pin`, and the folders of the actions you started most recently (up to 20, from Finder, the command line or Shortcuts), in a small file `state.toml` next to the settings file. Only your user account can read it. The Folders section of the setup window lists them. An AI assistant that you connect to Right Here over MCP can read them with the `right_here_bookmarks` tool, and what that assistant reads is handled under its own privacy practices. `rh unpin <folder>` removes a pin, and `rh recents --clear` empties the recent list (the Folders section does both). Config sync does not copy this file.
priv.stores.2: A small local log of recent actions and failures at `~/Library/Logs/right-here/rh.log`. It stays on your Mac, is never sent anywhere, and you can delete it at any time. Its size is limited and old entries are rotated out.
priv.events.title: Apple events
priv.events.body: To open a window in your terminal or to start a command you chose, Right Here sends Apple events to that terminal, and to Finder when you or an AI assistant ask what is selected. macOS asks for your permission the first time, and you can withdraw it in System Settings, Privacy & Security, Automation.
priv.other.title: Other apps you choose
priv.other.body: When Right Here opens a folder in another app or starts an AI agent, that app or agent has its own privacy practices. Right Here does not control them.
priv.children.title: Children
priv.children.body: Right Here collects no personal information from anyone, including children.
